title: This Dog Waited At A Train Station For 9 Years
description: An Akita named Hachi kept walking to Shibuya Station for nine and a half years after his owner died. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hachik%C5%8D Would your dog wait for you? #anime #shorts #animestory #retroanime #truestory #history

characters.Hachi: large cream-white Akita dog, thick fur, curled tail, dark gentle eyes, left ear drooping slightly, plain brown leather collar, no clothes
characters.Hidesaburo Ueno: 53-year-old Japanese agriculture professor in 1924, short graying hair, clean-shaven, no hat, dark gray 1920s wool suit, white high-collar shirt, black leather briefcase

scenes.say: An Akita named Hachi waited at Tokyo's Shibuya Station for nine and a half years. The man he was waiting for never once came back.
scenes.video: [0-4s] Outside the small wooden Shibuya Station building in 1930s Tokyo at dusk, Hachi sits alone by the entrance, a few commuters passing in the background. [4-7s] Close-up of Hachi's face, ears up, watching the station exit. [7-10s] Low shot from behind Hachi as a steam train pulls into the platform beyond the gate.

scenes.say: In 1924, professor Hidesaburo Ueno brought the puppy to Tokyo. Hachi slept under his bed, and every day he walked to Shibuya Station to meet Ueno's train home.
scenes.video: [0-4s] Inside Ueno's warm wooden house in Shibuya, 1924, Hidesaburo Ueno kneels and lifts a small fluffy cream-white Akita puppy. [4-7s] At night in Ueno's bedroom, young Hachi sleeps under a Western-style wooden bed. [7-10s] Outside Shibuya Station in the evening, Hidesaburo Ueno steps out of the gate smiling as Hachi runs to him.

scenes.say: But on May 21, 1925, Ueno died suddenly at work. Hachi vanished, and was found days later in a shed beside Ueno's shirt, not eating. They'd had fifteen months together.
scenes.video: [0-4s] Inside a quiet university office in Tokyo, 1925, Hidesaburo Ueno's empty chair beside his desk, his briefcase on the floor. [4-7s] Inside a dim wooden storage shed behind Ueno's house, Hachi lies curled beside a folded futon. [7-10s] Close-up of Hachi's still face, a full food bowl untouched in front of him.

scenes.say: So the day after the wake, Hachi walked back to Shibuya Station and waited for the train. Ueno wasn't on it. Hachi came back the next day anyway. And the next.
scenes.video: [0-4s] Hachi walks alone down a quiet dirt road in Shibuya toward the small wooden station. [4-7s] Outside Shibuya Station, Hachi sits by the exit as a few commuters walk past him. [7-10s] Same spot outside Shibuya Station, now in falling snow, Hachi still sitting and watching the exit.

scenes.say: He kept coming for years, even after mange took all his fur in 1929. Then in 1932 a newspaper told his story, and strangers started bringing him food at the station.
scenes.video: [0-4s] Outside Shibuya Station on a rainy day, a thin Hachi with patchy fur lies by the entrance. [4-7s] Outside Shibuya Station on a sunny morning, an older woman in a kimono crouches and sets a small bowl of food in front of Hachi. [7-10s] Close-up of a schoolboy gently petting Hachi's head, Hachi's eyes still on the station exit.

scenes.say: Hachi died on March 8, 1935, on a street in Shibuya. His funeral was held at Ueno's grave, so after nine and a half years of waiting, Hachi was finally with him.
scenes.video: [0-4s] A quiet alley entrance near a wooden gate in Shibuya at dawn, an old gray-muzzled Hachi lies peacefully. [4-7s] In Aoyama Cemetery under bare trees, a simple stone grave with fresh white flowers. [7-10s] Soft dream-like shot outside Shibuya Station at sunset: Hidesaburo Ueno steps out of the gate and young Hachi runs to him.
